newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Rubber prices fall at latest Colombo auction.
newsitem.headline: Rubber prices fall at latest Colombo auction.

text.p: Colombo rubber prices fell slightly at Thursday's auction as buyers and sellers could not agree on a price for the lower than average quantity on offer, brokers and exporters said.

"Buyers were looking at lower prices and sellers were unwilling to come down. Basically it was a stalemate and hardly any rubber got sold," said Amanda Weerasinghe, managing director of export firm Almar Trading Company.
"Overseas rubber prices are sluggish. Sri Lankan shippers too are fairly well covered. So there was no immediate demand from buyers," he said.

Best latex one-x, the purest grade, went unquoted from 75 rupees per kilo on Tuesday when the auction was last held. Number one was unchanged from Tuesday, fetching 73.75 rupees per kilo, while RSS 1 went unquoted on both days, brokers said.
On offer were 158 tonnes of crepe, compared to about 200 tonnes in previous weeks.
"Since auction prices were not acceptable to some sellers, they sold some quantities outside the auction," a broker for Forbes and Walker said.
